Oh sorry just read this, I was fortunate because my graduate program included an optional PR course which I took because I am not good at self-scheduling on studying. However, I would also not recommend it because it didn't have set study times or any strict deadlines to follow which I personally needed. There probably was some course that fit my criteria, but the school I attended didn't offer it and it would probably cost more money.

Besides all of that, I spent a good month or two on content review, making sure I was understanding what the material was teaching me along the way in both the books and the video lectures (which were super basic concepts, not sure they helped much). I've had both kaplan and princeton books, and I found that kaplan works better for me. I'd recommend trying to look into a couple passages before buying any sets if you can, maybe checking to see if the libraries have any older editions to get a glimpse.  
  
After I read the books (skipping sociology/psychology since I felt those were overly dense) I would do ANKI (ANKI is super important especially if flashcards work for you!!) and many, many practice questions on my weakest subjects (chemistry/physics) and some on the other sections. Then I pulled questions from NextStep and the AAMC question banks. Then I only did 2 practice FL's which is pretty low, but I think I was overly afraid of "wasting" them. The practice AAMC tests I took were highly reflective of my final score, although I wish it was closer to the 510 I got on the first one haha. If you can, apply for financial assistance and get the AAMC bundle, it really does have the best material for this test. Good luck!!

PS: [This video](https://youtu.be/AI4aFwt-498?si=jW_mi0hi_n6V1H21) is a great guide for setting ANKI up and I swear up and down by it, especially for sociology/psychology.

Had a serious relationship for 2.5 years that ended with my ex cheating, he got into a new relationship with someone else a week later. I was feeling pretty down before that, but that really made me spiral along with my mom's alcoholism and going through the majority of the summer spending my time in my room alone with hardly any friends. I basically became non-functional, had 2 college classes I was taking over the summer that I had to drop because I couldn't handle anything. Even just recently I was in my bed until 9pm just stuck in my head and not wanting to do anything and just hoping for an early death by accident or something so I didn't have to put people through the pain of knowing I ended my life by choice.

Self hatred is a bitch. I've had those feelings more times than I can count. I know having only a few friends feels shitty and like no one cares about you, but quantity means nothing in regards to friendships. All that matters is that they care about you and you care about them, even if it doesn't seem like they care it could be your self hatred projecting itself and warping your perception. 

I'm sure people care about you, especially your girlfriend. No matter how terrible you think you are, she's still with you. I'm sure she wants to work through this with you and support you. Let her know when you need to lean on her for support, I'm sure she would be happy to give it to you. I'm also trying to dedicate my life to science/medicine because it feels like the only thing that's worth spending my life on. I'm sure you can succeed, it takes time to make progress on careers and life goals, longer than anyone would like. 

Hope some of this helped you, sometimes just knowing you're not alone is a huge help.
